results.title: Impact and Benefits of Ergonomic Interventions at Workplace
results.content: ## Impact and Benefits of Ergonomic Interventions at Workplace. Ergonomic interventions focus on providing a work environment that promotes comfort, safety, and efficiency while reducing the risk of work-related injuries and health issues. This article explores the significance of ergonomic interventions and highlights some key strategies that organizations can implement to enhance workplace efficiency and employee well-being. Ergonomics is the science that aims to optimize the interaction between people and their work environments. By designing tasks, tools, and workstations to align with human capabilities, ergonomics minimizes the risk of musculoskeletal disorders, fatigue, and other occupational hazards. A fundamental aspect of ergonomic interventions is the design of workstations that prioritize comfort, efficiency, and health. Ergonomic interventions also encompass the use of anti-glare screens, footrests, and wrist supports to minimize strain and discomfort. Ergonomic interventions focus on educating workers about the importance of proper body alignment and provide guidance on adopting healthy postures during different tasks. The effective ergonomic interventions require comprehensive training and education programs. These initiatives ensure that employees understand the principles of ergonomics and are equipped with the knowledge to apply ergonomic practices in their daily work routines. Training sessions can cover topics such as correct lifting techniques, workstation ergonomics, and strategies to reduce physical and mental stress. By raising awareness and providing practical guidance, organizations empower their workforce to actively participate in maintaining a healthy and ergonomic work environment. Ergonomic interventions encompass the design and selection of user-friendly software, interfaces, and devices that minimize physical and cognitive strain. Organizations can then implement necessary changes, whether it be updating equipment, modifying work processes, or providing additional training, to optimize the ergonomic conditions for their employees. Ergonomic interventions play a vital role in creating a safe, productive, and employee-centric work environment. Through ergonomic workstation design, promoting correct posture and movement, comprehensive training, and technology integration, businesses can reduce the risk of work-related injuries and health issues while improving job satisfaction and productivity. Continuous evaluation and improvement ensure that ergonomic interventions remain effective and aligned with evolving work practices, ultimately benefiting both employees and organizations as a whole. **Citation:** Machado M (2023) Impact and Benefits of Ergonomic Interventions at Workplace.

results.title: Ergonomic Strategies for the Aging Workforce - Conference Chronicles
results.content: # Ergonomic Strategies for the Aging Workforce. Effective ergonomics help all employees, but even more so the aging workforce. In this session at RIMS 2024, Ariel Jenkins, Assistant Vice President of Risk Services at Safety National, highlighted trends related to aging American workers and ergonomic strategies to help keep them safe in the workplace. Workers over the age of 55 represent a large and essential segment of the American economy, and their influence is growing. * Some older workers are not in a position to retire, while roughly 20% of Americans have no plan to retire. With such a large population of older workers, it is essential that each organization’s risk management program addresses their on-the-job safety. The importance of ergonomics magnifies as we age due to years of exposure to biomechanical forces, so it can be an impactful area of focus. **To address these risks, consider the following ergonomic strategies:**. Analyze workers’ compensation loss data.** Analyze employee reports of discomfort to prioritize which specific work areas to assess for ergonomics issues and, subsequently, apply work redesign and other interventions where possible. Collaborate with ergonomists and/or risk control professionals.** If you do not know where to start, your insurance carrier’s risk control consultants likely have adequate ergonomics experience. Set defined expectations for both footwear and body mechanics.** Footwear expectations should be aligned with controlling risks of the walking, standing, or climbing work surfaces. Educate employees on ergonomic best practices.** Establish body mechanics methods by job description to help educate employees on how to handle objects manually with minimal impact to vulnerable areas of the body. Create an Ergonomics Steering Committee led by experienced employees to assess risk factors and solutions.** This should include stakeholders that can help influence and drive a culture of safety. Regardless of the methods of control, ergonomic interventions must be inclusive and accepted by the workforce to be effective. Onsite workers’ compensation triage and return to work transitioning on the job.** This can help reduce indemnity costs and tends to help injured employees recover and heal faster. * The Changing Landscape of Workers’ Compensation. * Workers’ Compensation and the Aging Workforce. * Gun Violence: Risk Management Strategies, Legal Landscape, and Cultural Change Initiatives.
